subject: Interim quota uplift request + grandfathered discount consideration
messages:
From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmetech.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@acmetech.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Spike this week — temporary quota uplift?

Tessa,

We saw an unexpected spike this week (new campaign) and are throttling at our current quota. Can Redwood do a temporary uplift for the next 10 days while we stabilize? We don’t want to commit to a larger monthly tier yet — this is strictly transient, but it’s material: estimated additional ~3M tokens/day for the period.

A couple of asks from our side:
- Can you confirm options and lead time for a short-term uplift?
- Is there a simple billing path (one-off true-up vs. short-term upgrade)?
- We also have an existing contract with a small customer discount that we expected to continue; if we accept a temporary uplift, would that discount be preserved (we refer to it as a ‘grandfathered’ price in our procurement notes)?

If you want raw usage I can share a CSV — otherwise a high-level response is fine. We’re trying to avoid production impact.

—Jordan
Jordan Miles
Head of Platform
Acme Tech
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmetech.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 09:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike this week — temporary quota uplift?

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the heads up and sorry you’re seeing throttling. Short answers up front:

- Yes, we can provision a temporary uplift for a fixed window (1–30 days) with two common billing paths: one-off true-up (post-period usage invoice) or a pro-rated short-term tier upgrade.
- Lead time: we can enable an uplift within 2 hours for emergency cases; formal provisioning and monitoring takes ~1 business day for capacity planning.
- Discount preservation: that depends on whether the uplift is handled as a true-up (you keep your current rate) or a tier upgrade (pricing follows the higher tier rate). We’ve allowed grandfathered rates in the past via an amendment/credit when we have an active committed relationship.

If you can share the June usage export (or an estimate), I’ll put together two brief options with numbers and a recommended path. Looping in Marcus + Vivek to weigh pricing and Laura for finance/credit treatment.

If you’d like immediate relief while we align on pricing, we can enable a temporary 10-day uplift now and true-up later — we’ll flag the account and apply guardrails so it doesn’t persist beyond the window.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmetech.com>
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike this week — temporary quota uplift?

Jordan / team — thanks for the context. I sketched three practical options and attached a one-page pricing worksheet (proposed_uplift_pricing_0728.xlsx). High level:

Option A — Emergency true-up (fastest)
- Enable 10-day uplift now (est +3M tokens/day)
- Post-period invoice for overage at current contracted per-token rate
- No change to existing contract or tier

Option B — Short-term tier (pro-rated)
- Move to higher short-term tier for 10 days (pro-rated monthly charge)
- Tier pricing is slightly higher than grandfathered rate but includes priority routing and a small burst discount (10%)
- Useful if you prefer predictable charge rather than an overage invoice

Option C — Uplift + grandfathered commitment credit (requires approval)
- We provision uplift and commit to preserve your current effective rate for 12 months via an amendment and administrative credit to offset uplift delta
- Requires approval from revenue leadership (Vivek) and a short amendment (DocuSign)

Numbers in the attachment assume a baseline of ~2M tokens/day and a burst to 5M. If you want a different baseline number I can recalc quickly.

Recommendations: for speed, Option A now + follow up with Option C if Acme wants price protection. If Acme is sensitive to invoice timing, Option B is cleaner but slightly more expensive in unit cost.

—Marcus
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmetech.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@acmetech.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 08:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike this week — temporary quota uplift?

Thanks Marcus — Option B is clean but we’d prefer Option C if possible: preserve our negotiated effective rate for 12 months. That’s important for procurement. We’re willing to sign a short amendment now that covers the price-protection period and the temporary uplift.

Two quick asks:
1) Can Redwood confirm the credit or offset amount in dollars so procurement can include it in the PO?
2) Timeline to get a DocuSign amendment in-hand? We need it before end of week to get internal approvals.

I’ll attach a short usage export from our side if that helps.

—Jordan
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Miles <jordan.miles@acmetech.com>
Date: Wed, 29 Jul 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike this week — temporary quota uplift?

Vivek — Jordan at Acme is asking for Option C (12-month price protection + temporary uplift). I’ve attached their usage file (usage_report_Jun2026.csv) and Marcus’s pricing worksheet. Requested timeline: amendment signed by EOW.

Can you approve an administrative credit equal to the uplift delta (we estimate ~$18k) to be applied as a 12-month monthly amortized credit against invoices, or do you want to propose a different mechanism? If approved, legal can spin an amendment and we push through DocuSign ASAP.

If you prefer, we can do a smaller fixed credit and re-evaluate at renewal — I noted a few ways in the attached worksheet.

—Tessa
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Spike this week — temporary quota uplift?

Approved.

We will:
- Provision the 10-day uplift immediately (ops notified).
- Apply an administrative credit of $18,000 amortized over 12 months to preserve the current effective unit rate for Acme.
- Legal: please prepare a short amendment reflecting the 12-month price protection and the uplift window. Aim for DocuSign link in <24 hours.

Marcus/Laura — confirm accounting impact and that the credit mechanism is processed as an AR adjustment. Tessa — please send Jordan the DocuSign once ready and confirm uplift is live.

—Vivek Kulkarni
SVP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
